response: Numerous studies have found that taxation is one of the most effective policy instruments for tobacco control. However, in countries with market economies, increases in the cigarette tax rate can be linked to cigarette retail prices. But, in the case of China, which has a non-market economy and a tobacco monopoly system, tax increases do not necessarily get passed on to the retail price. This means that the relationship between cigarette tax rates and retail prices may vary depending on the economic system and tobacco industry structure of a given country.
